80: INTRODUCTION
81: 
82: This Bulletin contains statistics of the United States Government transactions and other information gathered by the Treasury Department. It is the intention to issue similar Bulletins monthly and to incorporate in them information additional to that which is included in this first issue.
83: 
84: The purpose of the Bulletin is to extend knowledge of the public finances, monetary developments and activities of the Treasury Department by making information available in a more compact and usable form. The material herein contained supplements or recapitulates data contained in the Daily Treasury Statement and other publications and press releases of the Treasury Department.
85: 
86: Only a limited number of copies is being prepared, for the present distribution will be restricted in the main to periodical publications desiring to make use of the material and to public officers. Other requests may be filled only to the extent of the limited supply.
87: 
88: I shall be glad to receive and to give careful consideration to suggestions for improving the Bulletin so as to make it serve its purpose more adequately.
89: 
90: Henry Morgenthau, Jr. Secretary of the Treasury.

steps.message:
Based on the Treasury Bulletin data for the period Jan. 2, 1935 - Jan. 1, 1936 (representing the 1935 calendar year), the gold bloc countries at the start of 1935 were France, Italy, Netherlands, and Switzerland (excluding Belgium, Poland, and Luxembourg per your instructions).

The net capital movement values (in thousands of dollars) for these countries:
- France: 177,610
- Italy: 21,011
- Netherlands: 55,362
- Switzerland: 73,990

Total: 327,973 thousand dollars = 0.327973 billion dollars

Rounded to the nearest thousandths place: **0.328 billion dollars**
